name: Eye color meditation / visualization
summary: Trying to change iris color by meditating or picturing a new shade; no study has tested it and iris color is set by melanin and genes.
lead: Eye color meditation or visualization is a practice in which people try to change the color of their irises by meditating, affirming or mentally picturing a different color. It circulates in wellness and self-transformation circles and in some appearance-focused online communities as a non-invasive alternative to cosmetic lenses or surgical procedures.

name: Eye color diet
summary: Food and supplement routines said to lighten the eyes; iris color is set by melanin and genes and no trial has tested diet.
lead: The eye color diet refers to claims that particular foods, supplements, hydration habits or eating patterns can lighten or otherwise change the color of the iris. It appears in wellness content and appearance-focused online discussion as a way to alter eye color without lenses or procedures.

name: Limbal ring contact lenses
summary: Tinted contacts that add a dark rim to the iris for a younger, more striking look; the ring itself has attractiveness studies, the lenses do not.
lead: Limbal ring contact lenses are cosmetic soft lenses printed with a dark band at the outer edge of the iris, imitating a prominent limbal ring. Some designs only darken the iris border, while others (often called circle lenses) extend the dark rim outward so the iris appears larger .
claims: A dark limbal ring makes eyes look healthier and more striking.
Lenses that add only a limbal ring can supply the look.

name: Limbal ring theory
summary: The idea that a dark ring around the iris signals youth and health; small perception studies support it, forums treat it as a major eye feature.
lead: Limbal ring theory is the idea, common in looksmaxxing and attractiveness discussions, that the dark ring around the iris signals youth and health, and that a prominent ring therefore makes a face more attractive. The limbal ring is the darker band visible where the iris meets the white of the eye (the sclera), at the corneal limbus .
claims: A dark limbal ring makes eyes look more striking and is a big looks factor.
The ring signals health and youth.
Body sulfur levels determine how thick or dark the ring is.
Contact lenses can add a limbal ring to eyes that lack one.

name: Brimonidine drops (Lumify)
summary: Low-dose OTC brimonidine drops that shrink eye-surface vessels for whiter-looking sclera; FDA-cleared for redness, untested as a cosmetic.
lead: Brimonidine is an alpha-2 adrenergic agonist used in prescription eye drops to lower eye pressure in glaucoma and ocular hypertension, and as a topical gel that reduces facial redness in rosacea . At a low concentration of 0.025 percent it is sold over the counter as Lumify, made by Bausch + Lomb, for temporary relief of eye redness from minor irritations .
claims: Lumify whitens the sclera by shrinking blood vessels.
Lumify changes light eyes to a different shade such as hazel.
Lumify rebounds less than Visine, so alternating the two avoids tolerance.

name: Tetrahydrozoline drops (Visine)
summary: OTC redness drops (0.05% tetrahydrozoline) that whiten the sclera fast, with well-known rebound redness on repeated use.
lead: Tetrahydrozoline (also spelled tetryzoline) is an over-the-counter vasoconstrictor used in eye drops and nasal sprays. The best-known redness-relief eye drop containing it is Visine, which contains 0.05 percent tetrahydrozoline hydrochloride and is sold to temporarily relieve eye redness from minor irritations .
claims: Redness drops with tetrahydrozoline whiten the eyes quickly.
Visine causes rebound redness and is stronger than Lumify.
Alternating Visine and Lumify avoids tolerance.

name: Artificial tears
summary: Over-the-counter lubricating eye drops for dry, irritated eyes: standard first-line comfort care, not a whitening or redness fix.
lead: Artificial tears are lubricating eye drops, gels and ointments that are designed to relieve dryness and irritation of the ocular surface. They are sold mostly over the counter and are used mainly for dry eye disease, for contact lens comfort and during or after some eye procedures .

name: Scleral whitening / conjunctivectomy
summary: Elective surgery that removes or cauterises conjunctival tissue to make the whites of the eyes look whiter; published reports are limited to case reports of late complications.
lead: Scleral whitening, also called cosmetic eye whitening or cosmetic conjunctivectomy, is an elective procedure intended to make the white of the eye appear whiter by removing or treating the conjunctival tissue and its blood vessels. One commercially named version is I-BRITE .

name: Pinguecula / pterygium removal
summary: Surgery to remove the yellowish or pinkish conjunctival growths of pinguecula and pterygium, done mainly for medical reasons and sometimes for looks.
lead: A pinguecula is a yellowish raised area of the conjunctiva, and a pterygium is a related triangular growth that extends from the conjunctiva onto the cornea. Both are associated with ultraviolet light and dust exposure; a pterygium is sometimes called surfer's eye .

name: Antihistamine eye drops
summary: Allergy eye drops such as olopatadine and ketotifen that treat itchy, red allergic eyes; some brands pair an antihistamine with a redness-reliever.
lead: Antihistamine eye drops are topical medicines for allergic conjunctivitis, a reaction to allergens such as pollen, animal dander, dust mites or cosmetics that causes itching, redness, tearing and eyelid swelling .

name: Hypochlorous acid lid spray
summary: A hypochlorous acid eyelid cleanser used for lid hygiene in blepharitis and redness; supporting data is small and mostly indirect.
lead: Hypochlorous acid (HOCl) is a weak acid formed when chlorine dissolves in water, and it is the main disinfecting agent in chlorine solutions. White blood cells produce it naturally to fight microbes . Commercial eyelid sprays and wipes use stabilised solutions for lid hygiene.

name: Warm compress / meibomian care
summary: Heating the eyelids to loosen oil blockages in the meibomian glands, a standard first step for blepharitis and evaporative dry eye with a modest research base.
lead: A warm compress applies moist or dry heat, commonly through a heated cloth, gel mask or electric device, to the closed eyelids. It is a long-standing conservative treatment for meibomian gland dysfunction (MGD), the leading cause of evaporative dry eye, which is marked by blocked gland ducts and altered oil secretion that destabilise the tear film .

name: Baby shampoo lid scrubs
summary: Diluted baby shampoo on the lash line: an old blepharitis hygiene routine, studied for lid disease rather than looks.
lead: Baby shampoo lid scrubs are a form of eyelid hygiene in which diluted tear-free baby shampoo is used to clean the lash line. The practice is long associated with the management of blepharitis, an inflammation of the eyelid margin, and is also discussed in appearance contexts as a way to reduce lid redness and crusting around the eyes.

name: Cold compress for red eyes
summary: A chilled cloth on the eyes for a quick depuff; tested only in allergic itch, not for looks.
lead: A cold compress for red eyes is the application of a chilled cloth, pack or similar object to the closed eyelids or face to reduce redness and puffiness for a short time. It is discussed as a quick appearance fix and as a comfort measure in some forms of eye irritation.

name: 20-20-20 rule / screen breaks
summary: Look 20 feet away for 20 seconds every 20 minutes: a free screen habit aimed at eye strain, not eye whiteness.
lead: The 20-20-20 rule is a commonly cited habit for screen users: every 20 minutes, look at something about 20 feet (6 metres) away for 20 seconds. It is promoted as a way to reduce digital eye strain, with tired, dry or red eyes often named among the symptoms.

name: Blue-light glasses
summary: Light-filtering lenses sold for screen strain and sleep; the 'brighter eyes' claim has not been studied.
lead: Blue-light glasses, also called blue-blocking or blue-filtering glasses, are spectacles with lenses that filter part of the blue end of visible light emitted by screens and LED lighting. They are sold over the counter, often with clear lenses and fashion frames, and marketed for digital eye strain and sleep. In appearance forums they are also claimed to make eyes look brighter or less tired.

name: Lutein and zeaxanthin supplements
summary: Plant carotenoids sold for eye health; the research is about macular degeneration, not cosmetic eye brightness, and its overall result there is modest.
lead: Lutein and zeaxanthin are xanthophyll carotenoids, yellow pigments made by plants and obtained by people from foods such as leafy greens and egg yolks. They are isomers that the body can interconvert, and they accumulate in the macula of the retina . Supplements combining the two are marketed mainly for eye health and are a large segment of the dietary-supplement market .

name: Bilberry extract
summary: Anthocyanin-rich European blueberry extract with a folk reputation for vision; trials are small and no cosmetic eye-brightening evidence exists.
lead: Bilberry (Vaccinium myrtillus) is a low-growing shrub native to northern Europe, with dark blue-black berries that are eaten fresh and processed into jams, liqueurs and dried powders or standardised extracts sold as dietary supplements . The berries are rich in anthocyanins, along with other polyphenols and tannins .

name: Vitamin A for eyes
summary: Essential for vision and the eye surface; deficiency causes night blindness and dry eye, but evidence for extra vitamin A in well-nourished people is thin and excess is toxic.
lead: Vitamin A is a fat-soluble vitamin required for vision and for maintaining the surface tissues of the eye. It is needed to rebuild rhodopsin, the pigment in rod cells; deficiency first shows as night blindness and, when severe, as xerophthalmia, in which the conjunctiva and cornea dry out, Bitot's spots may form and the cornea can ulcerate . Vitamin A deficiency is described as the leading cause of preventable childhood blindness .

name: Liver detox for yellow sclera
summary: The belief that a liver cleanse can whiten yellowish eye whites; medical sources tie true yellowing to bilirubin and advise evaluation.
lead: Liver detox for yellow sclera is a belief that yellowish or dull eye whites indicate a burdened liver and can be whitened by cleansing diets, herbs or supplements. No published study has tested a detox regimen for eye whiteness.

name: Castor oil eye drops
summary: A folk practice of putting castor oil in the eyes for clarity or brightness; no studies of raw oil for this exist.
lead: Castor oil eye drops is a folk practice in which oil pressed from the seeds of Ricinus communis is placed in the eyes, with claims of soothing or brightening them. No published study of unformulated castor oil for this purpose was found.

name: Hydrogen peroxide eye drops
summary: Putting hydrogen peroxide in the eyes to whiten them; reference sources warn that even 3 percent can injure the eye.
lead: Hydrogen peroxide eye drops refers to applying hydrogen peroxide solution directly to the eye, sometimes with the aim of whitening or cleansing it. It is not a medically recognised treatment for that purpose, and no published studies of it for appearance were found.

name: Nude / white waterline eyeliner
summary: Pale pencil on the lower waterline, said to brighten the eyes; popular tip, no studies behind it.
lead: Nude or white waterline eyeliner is a makeup practice in which a light-colored (skin-toned, beige or white) pencil is applied to the lower waterline, the inner rim of the lower eyelid. Practitioners in appearance communities say it makes the eyes look brighter, more awake and larger.

name: Dark eyeliner to make iris pop
summary: Dark liner around the eye to contrast the iris and make its color look brighter; a makeup tip with no studies.
lead: Dark eyeliner to make the iris pop is a makeup practice in which dark liner is applied along the lash line to increase contrast with the iris. Practitioners say it makes eye color look more vivid.

name: Sclera tattoo (eyeball tattooing)
summary: Injecting ink into the white of the eye to change its color; permanent, with case reports of serious vision-threatening complications.
lead: Scleral tattooing is the injection of pigment into the sclera, the white of the eye, to change its color permanently. Wikipedia reports no documented cosmetic use before the early 21st century; the modern practice is credited to body-modification enthusiast Shannon Larratt and practitioner Howie "Luna Cobra" Rollins around 2007.

name: Redness-minimizing ring light
summary: A ring light gives even, shadow-light face lighting for photos; its effect on redness is untested.
lead: A ring light is a circular lighting device, usually a ring of LEDs, that surrounds a camera lens or smartphone and lights the subject from nearly all sides. Descriptions of the product say it produces even, low-shadow illumination and a ring-shaped reflection (catchlight) in the eyes. In looksmaxxing discussion the idea of a "redness-minimizing" ring light refers to using this kind of lighting, often with adjustable colour temperature, to make skin tone and the eyes look more even and brighter in photos and video.
claims: A ring light evens out skin tone and reduces visible shadows and blemishes on camera.
The ring catchlight makes the eyes look brighter.

name: Eye makeup remover & sleep for dark circles
summary: Removing eye makeup and sleeping well is the baseline dark-circle habit forums cite; no study tests it.
lead: This entry covers the lifestyle approach, discussed in looksmaxxing communities, of removing eye makeup before bed and getting adequate sleep as a way to reduce the appearance of dark circles under the eyes. Forum users treat sleep hygiene and hydration as basic first steps before products or procedures.
claims: Better sleep timing and hydration can clear dark circles.
Dark circles are genetic or structural, so lifestyle changes do not help and fillers or grafting are needed.

name: Colored sunglasses lenses
summary: Tinted sunglasses are a style choice; research covers contrast and light sensitivity, not looks.
lead: Colored sunglasses lenses are tinted lenses, such as yellow, orange, rose or blue, worn mainly for style in looksmaxxing and fashion contexts. A tint changes the colour of the wearer's view and, depending on the colour, can alter contrast and colour discrimination.

name: Red light therapy for eyes
summary: Red light for the eye area is claimed to brighten; cosmetic evidence is absent and myopia studies are separate.
lead: Red light therapy, also called low-level laser therapy or photobiomodulation, applies low-power red or near-infrared light from lasers or LEDs to the body. Wikipedia describes its effectiveness as under investigation and notes that the generally accepted theory involves an enzyme in mitochondria.

name: Under-eye concealer
summary: Concealer masks under-eye darkness for the day; it is cosmetic camouflage with no treatment effect.
lead: Under-eye concealer is a pigmented cosmetic applied to the skin beneath the eyes to mask dark circles, redness or discolouration. Grokipedia describes concealer as thicker and more pigmented than foundation and intended for small areas.
claims: Concealer can hide dark circles without looking like makeup.
Concealer is a hard-to-obtain item for men because of social stigma.
